subject.title: fix(qqbot): bound remote media downloads with header and idle timeouts

question: Should QQBot adopt the shared 30-second no-progress timeout as the default for all adapter and file-utility remote-media downloads, accepting that exceptionally slow transfers with no chunk for 30 seconds now fail?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes runtime failure behavior for existing QQBot deployments; the submitted proof supports the intended behavior, but accepting the availability-versus-hang tradeoff is an owner decision.

options.title: Adopt the shared default
options.body: Accept the 120-second header and 30-second body-idle defaults after the QQBot owner confirms they match the channel's supported media-transfer behavior.

options.title: Narrow the policy
options.body: Keep the bounded-reader fix but restrict or alter the default if a QQBot-specific caller has a legitimate longer no-progress contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt the shared default
recommendation.body: Accept the 120-second header and 30-second body-idle defaults after the QQBot owner confirms they match the channel's supported media-transfer behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: A source and history pass is needed to identify the current QQBot-area owner rather than inferring ownership from the contributor branch.
